messages:
maria: Heads-up — our JS SDK sample app failed after deploying to Vercel Edge. Error in logs: `ReferenceError: require is not defined`. Local node run (v18) works fine.

ken: That screams CJS landed in the bundle. What's package.json look like (type/exports/main)?

maria: package.json currently: `type: \"module\"`, `main: \"dist/index.cjs.js\"`, `exports` has `import: ./dist/index.mjs` and `require: ./dist/index.cjs.js`. We built a separate `dist/edge/index.mjs` but didn't export it.

tess: Edge runtimes (Vercel, CF) require pure ESM and no node builtins. If any file in the published tarball contains `require()` or `module.exports` esbuild may inline it. Did any dependency get bundled?

maria: Our auth/retry uses `const fetch = globalThis.fetch || require('node-fetch')` to support node. That `require` is exactly what blows up.

ken: Avoid runtime `require` for cross-runtime code. Options: 1) use dynamic import with feature gating `await import('node-fetch')` inside a Node-only wrapper, 2) accept `fetch` as an injected dependency (options param), or 3) provide two clearly exported entrypoints (node vs edge).

maria: For immediate fix I replaced inline require with a tiny helper `getFetch()` that does: if (typeof globalThis.fetch === 'function') return globalThis.fetch; if (process && process.versions && process.versions.node) { return (await import('node-fetch')).default } else throw. But that dynamic import still causes packagers to include node-fetch sometimes.

tess: Dynamic import is better but bundlers can still tree-shake oddly. Publishing a dedicated `./edge` subpath that points to an ESM-only bundle with zero node polyfills gives the cleanest runtime contract. Consumers deploying to edge can import `@redwood/sdk/edge`.

ken: But we want minimal DX friction. Splitting packages (sdk & sdk-edge) gives clarity but doubles release surface. Subpath export keeps single package and works with conditional exports for types too. Example exports: 
```
"exports": {
  "./edge": {"import": "./dist/edge/index.mjs", "types": "./dist/edge/index.d.ts"},
  "./": {"import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs.js", "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"}
}
```
This makes `import '@redwood/sdk/edge'` explicit.

maria: Yeah that solves the require problem and ensures edge builds don't accidentally include node shims. But we need to ensure TypeScript resolves types correctly: `types` per export path is necessary. Also add `typesVersions` if consumers use `paths` mapping.

tess: CI-wise we should add a Vercel/edge smoke job that does minimal build+deploy check and runs sample app health endpoint. Also add an esbuild bundle check that simulates bundler resolution. Catch these before publish.

ken: Action items: 1) Add `dist/edge` ESM-only build target (no node polyfills). 2) Update package.json exports with `./edge` subpath and per-subpath `types`. 3) Refactor auth/retry to accept a `fetch` adapter as arg and avoid inline requires. 4) Update sample app docs: "For edge deploys import '@redwood/sdk/edge' or set bundler alias to dist/edge." 5) Add CI matrix row for edge.

maria: I'll open PR `edge-entrypoint-and-fetch-adapter` with those changes and a minimal Vercel CI sample.

build-bot: :package: built package 0.13.0-edge-preview and published tag `edge-preview`.

pkg-manager: FYI we should also test downstream frameworks (Next.js, Remix) because some bundle optimizers rewrite conditional exports. Add a small test with Next/ISR that imports edge subpath.

maria: good call. I'll add a Next sample to the CI matrix. Thanks!
